content:
Yesterday we saw the golden spoon kaph, the palm of a hand filled with pure incense and brought to the altar by each of the twelve leaders. We saw that gold speaks of divine character, that incense represents prayer and worship, that the twelve golden spoons point to the twelve apostolic foundations through which the prayers of all God’s people are carried through Christ before the throne.

We also saw that the spoon did not produce the incense; it simply carried what was placed in it and that we too are vessels, carrying the fragrance of Christ that Yahweh places in us. Today we study the weight: 10 shekels per spoon, 120 shekels total. And the number 120 opens a door into one of the most significant patterns in all of Scripture.

The golden spoon weighed 10 shekels. Ten in Scripture is the number of completeness in the context of responsibility and accountability before God. The Ten Commandments; the complete moral law of God given to humanity. The ten plagues; the complete judgment on Egypt before the redemption of Israel. The ten virgins of Matthew 25; the complete picture of those who wait for the bridegroom. In each case, ten marks out the full measure of what is required or expected. The golden spoon at 10 shekels says that the prayer and worship we bring to God is not a partial matter. It is the full measure of what He expects from a covenant people. Not occasional prayer. Not prayer when convenient. The complete, full, daily offering of worship before His face.

And when we multiply 10 by 12 the ten shekels of each spoon by the twelve leaders we arrive at 120 shekels of gold in total. One hundred and twenty is the number that appears at three of the most decisive transition moments in all of Scripture, and it is not by accident that the total weight of the golden incense spoons lands exactly on this number.

The first time the number 120 appears in connection with a major turning point is in Genesis 6:3, where Yahweh says: “My Spirit shall not abide in man forever, for he is flesh: his days shall be 120 years.” This was spoken before the flood before the judgment and the new beginning that followed. One hundred and twenty years of warning, of preparation, of building the ark. And then the old world ended and a new world began. The 120 stood at the threshold between the world that was and the world that came after.

The second appearance is in the life of Moses. Deuteronomy 34:7 says: “Moses was 120 years old when he died. His eye was undimmed and his vigour unabated.” Moses died at exactly 120 years; complete in his course, full in his strength, not diminished. He was a type of Christ throughout his ministry; the prophet like Moses who was to come (Deuteronomy 18:15). And as Moses died at 120 and Joshua led Israel into the inheritance, so Christ completed His earthly course and the Spirit led the new creation assembly into its inheritance. The 120 of Moses’ life marks the completion of one leader and the beginning of the next.

The third and most direct appearance is in Acts 1:15, just before the Day of Pentecost: “In those days Peter stood up among the brothers; the company of persons was in all about 120.” One hundred and twenty disciples, gathered together in the upper room, waiting. They had been with Christ. They had received the command to wait for the promise of the Father. And the 120 were the prepared, ready, waiting people on whom the Holy Spirit descended at Pentecost and through whom the new covenant witness to the world began. The 120 shekels of gold in the dedication offerings are pointing at exactly this moment; a complete and prepared people, full of prayer and worship, standing on the threshold of a new move of God.

When we put the three elements together; gold, incense, and the number 120 a single picture emerges with great clarity. Gold speaks of divine purity, faith and character. Incense speaks of the prayer and worship of a consecrated people. And 120 speaks of a people who are complete, prepared, and standing at the threshold of a new work of God. The 120 shekels of golden incense in the dedication offerings of Numbers 7 are a picture of the full, complete, prepared worshipping people of God who stand ready for the Spirit to move. Not a half-prepared people. Not a people who have some of the incense but not all.
One hundred and twenty shekels. Every gram of gold present. Every measure of incense offered. A complete and ready people before the face of Yahweh.

This speaks directly to the new creation assembly today. The church is being prepared. The 120 of the upper room was not the final count; it was the beginning of a harvest that is still being gathered. But the pattern of the 120 calls us to the same posture: a people who have completed what the previous season required, who are not still carrying the unfinished business of old covenants, old bitterness’s, and old half-surrenders, but who are gathered together in prayer and worship and expectation, carrying the golden incense before the face of Yahweh, ready for what He is about to do next.

The golden spoon of our lives must not be empty when the Spirit moves. When God is ready to do a new thing, He looks for the 120 the prepared, praying, worshipping, consecrated people who have been filling the golden palm of their lives with incense day after day, in the hidden place, before the known audience of one. The dedication of the altar in Numbers 7 led to the voice from between the cherubim in verse 89. The 120 disciples in the upper room led to the sound of a rushing mighty wind in Acts 2. The golden incense carried faithfully to the altar leads to the presence of God filling the house. This is the invitation the 120 shekels extend to every new creation believer: be the golden spoon, stay filled with incense, carry the fragrance to the altar daily, and wait for the voice.

title: Prayer
text:
Yahweh, You are the God who receives the fragrance of prayer. You did not ask us to Yahweh, You are the God who fills the prepared vessel and moves among a ready people. We thank You for the 120; for the pattern of a people who completed their course, who gathered together in prayer, and on whom Your Spirit descended with power. We want to be that people. We want to carry the golden spoon with the full 10 shekels not half a measure of prayer, not occasional worship, but the complete, daily, faithful offering of incense before Your presence. Forgive us for the times the spoon has been empty, for the seasons when we came before You without fragrance. Fill us again with the incense. Make us a people who are complete and prepared not still unfinished, so that when You are ready to move, like the 120 in the upper room, already on our knees, already carrying the fragrance, already waiting for the sound of the wind. Let the altar be filled with the golden incense of our worship.
And then let the voice speak. In Christ’s name, amen.
